target_review.notes: The frozen target preserves the approved nontrivial interpretation and its interior-time, integrability, differentiability, and energy conclusions. But the specification's full_target is only a compressed paraphrase: it omits the explicit quantifier/details of H003, the definition of a and the unit q condition, and the precise Lebesgue/Frobenius and no-endpoint conventions. More importantly, the proof graph's N003 derivation has an unsupported coordinate-change step: M010 only states measure preservation of the coordinate reindexing; R004 asserts this makes the original whole-space integral equal to the product-measure integral, without a listed theorem or a derivation of integral invariance. M003 then applies to the product measure, not by itself to the original integral. Thus AND closure to P is not established.

D001.notes: The intended energy density is stated, and its basic notation is consistent with the frozen target. The definition omits explicit argument bindings in the formula for u_t and ∂xj u and does not itself spell out the Euclidean/Frobenius convention; that convention is in the frozen target, not fully in this D entry. No hidden theorem is apparent.

D002.notes: Defines E as the Lebesgue integral of the already-defined density, with dependency D001 and the positive-time binder. Integrability is not assumed in the definition and is separately required/proved in the target.

D003.notes: The intended componentwise spatial Laplacian agrees with the frozen target, and no result is hidden in the definition. The type is only 'operator' and does not record its domain/codomain or bound spatial index; thus the definition ledger is incomplete as a type/domain declaration.

M001.notes: The supplied signature evidence records a successful full-telescope probe, theorem kind, commit, source hash, and axioms. The restatement is broadly faithful to the signature, including measurable-space/topological-space, normed additive commutative group, opens measurable, and finite measure on compacts. I inspected the pinned file only at its opening lines, not the declaration/source context, so the required official-source audit is incomplete. Its R002 application is plausible: e(.,t) is continuous with compact support and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets.

M003.notes: Probe gives the full telescope, including SFinite measures, normed additive commutative group, real normed-space structure, and product integrability, plus axioms. The application identifies the product integral step, but the source file itself was not read. Separately, M003 does not supply the missing conversion from the original spatial integral to the reindexed product integral.

M004.notes: Probe includes compactness and continuity hypotheses and complete outer telescope, but the pinned source was not read. The R003 use is conceptually consistent with uniform continuity on compact C×J; this source review remains incomplete.

M005.notes: Probe signature and application match the compact-product theorem, with topological-space instances and compactness of C and J accounted for. Pinned source was not read, so source fidelity is not established.

M006.notes: Signature records all central hypotheses: neighborhood, eventual a.e. strong measurability, base integrability, derivative measurability, a.e. uniform bound on the neighborhood, integrable bound, and a.e. pointwise HasDerivAt; also required RCLike/normed structures. The submitted restatement is broadly faithful. The official source was not read. Applicability merits caution: the interval used in the bound needs to be the theorem's neighborhood set and domination is required almost everywhere in x for every parameter in that set.

M007.notes: Probe signature supports the stated integration-by-parts identity with continuous-on-closed-interval, interior HasDerivAt, and interval-integrability conditions, in a complete normed algebra. The actual source was not read. The argument's chosen scalar g_j and constant 1 fit the algebra condition in principle, but the line interval/support bound is not explicitly constructed in the proof prose.

M008.notes: Probe reveals the actual theorem uses auto-parameters for μ(s)≠∞ and enorm(C)≠∞, which the restatement summarizes as finite measure and finite extended norm. Application gives grounds for both. Pinned source was not read; the exact auto-parameter conditions remain source-audit items.

M009.notes: Full probe signature says IntegrableOn f s μ plus MeasurableSet s imply integrability of the set indicator, matching the restatement. Application cites M008 and compact measurability. Pinned source was not read.

M010.notes: Probe signature is a MeasurePreserving result for piCongrLeft with Fintype indices, coordinate MeasureSpace instances, and coordinate volume sigma-finiteness. The submitted statement compresses these conditions and the source itself was not read. The application also overclaims what this theorem directly yields: measure preservation alone is not the equality of integrals claimed in R004 without an integral-invariance result or proof.

structure_review.notes: The visible graph has one target and producers for each internal node; retained roots and intermediate nodes are placed on the apparent backward dependency closure, with original H001-H003 retained. Nevertheless, AND-closure cannot accept N003: its R004 proof invokes M010 and then identifies the original integral with the product integral without a direct theorem establishing integral invariance under the measure-preserving equivalence or a local proof. Consequently R001 cannot validly close P. This is a global/source audit finding; no per-inference packet replay is claimed.

findings.finding: Unsupported integral change under coordinate reindexing in R004: M010 establishes measure preservation, but R004 uses it as equality of integrals on the reindexed product space. M003 only relates product and iterated integrals once product integrability is known; it does not establish the missing integral-invariance equality.
premises: M010 as restated and probed: coordinate reindexing is measure preserving
M003: product-integrable function's product integral equals its iterated integral
findings.unsupported_conclusion: The original whole-space integral of ∂j g_j equals the iterated integral in the reindexed coordinates.

findings.finding: Pinned official source files were not fully inspected for M001 and not inspected for the remaining M declarations. The full-signature evidence is valuable but does not substitute for source fidelity/applicability audit. No M review is represented as PASS.
